title: One App lifecycle
scope: Repository guide: startup, module updates and request rendering
evidence: The guide separates startup/module-map validation, subsequent module polling and the request-specific data/render lifecycle.
Inspected at commit 7a8181ddb3893ababd8bd26c76b4f1773931149c.
limitations: A public framework guide is not evidence that this exact revision runs in current Amex payment processing.
Its Express wording differs from the inspected request code's Fastify types; the report does not infer a single current server framework from this guide.

title: One App loadModules implementation
scope: Source code: module-map hashing, registry update, rejected-module handling and root configuration
evidence: The function hashes a fetched module map, updates the module registry, records rejected modules and refreshes client map/CSP state for applicable loaded modules.
Inspected at commit 7a8181ddb3893ababd8bd26c76b4f1773931149c.
limitations: This establishes code behavior at the revision, not a deployment topology, release-security guarantee or account authorization mechanism.

title: One App createRequestStore implementation
scope: Source code: per-request Holocron store, request-bound fetch and server/client configuration
evidence: The function constructs server state and client initial-state inputs, creates a request-bound fetch client and attaches a new Holocron store to the request.
Inspected at commit 7a8181ddb3893ababd8bd26c76b4f1773931149c.
limitations: Downstream serialization and the complete safeRequest/stateConfig implementations were not audited; this file alone cannot prove secret exclusion or tenant isolation.

title: One App API-call guide
scope: Repository guide and sample code: server/client data loading and shared fetch cache
evidence: The guide describes loadModuleData and fetchClient, then Fetchye/One App provider and cache integration for reuse of requests across modules.
Inspected at commit 7a8181ddb3893ababd8bd26c76b4f1773931149c.
limitations: The books API is illustrative. The examples do not establish an Amex issuer backend, authorization policy or production payment API.

title: Flowret runtime service Rts
scope: Source code: case start/resume, case-linked journey persistence and lifecycle/SLA hooks
evidence: startCase writes journey data under a case key; resumeCase reloads persisted case context. The runtime accepts host-provided component, event, storage and SLA interfaces.
Inspected at commit 1449bebe1051dd09a268735a982aad350e1280cb.
limitations: Case-linked persistence is not proof of immutable version enforcement or atomic coupling to a financial ledger.
No reviewed source establishes which current Amex production payment system deploys this engine.

title: Flowret persistence interface FlowretDao
evidence: The interface exposes write(key, Document), read(key) and incrCounter(key); it declares no multi-record transaction or conditional-write operation.
Inspected at commit 1449bebe1051dd09a268735a982aad350e1280cb.
limitations: Absence of an explicit interface guarantee does not establish a defect in any particular DAO implementation. Host storage and concurrency semantics require separate verification.

title: Flowret execution task and persist-step behavior
scope: Source code: response-state handling, parallel paths, persistence callbacks and error workbasket
evidence: processPersist invokes ON_PERSIST; an exception sets ERROR_PEND and the configured error workbasket. Parallel-route handling updates process state and audit before executing branches.
Inspected at commit 1449bebe1051dd09a268735a982aad350e1280cb.
limitations: JVM locks do not demonstrate cross-process serialization. Audit/process-state writes depend on configuration and host storage; external effects are not thereby exactly once.

title: Synapse architecture README
scope: Repository architecture: business, client/data, subscriber/publisher and utility boundaries
evidence: The README describes HTTP/business/subscriber responsibilities, external-service clients, resource access, publishers and cross-cutting utilities. It names Spring WebFlux/Netty reactive support and a Spring Web option.
Inspected at commit ea981729a13e7e56a8d678c9292c6e00c3bbcf61.
limitations: The architecture is a toolkit description, not a verified inventory of every Amex service. The referenced architecture image was not independently inspected; findings use the README text.

title: Synapse reactive create controller
scope: Source code: Spring HTTP controller using Reactive Streams and Reactor
evidence: The controller imports Reactive Streams Publisher and Reactor Mono; its POST create method delegates to execute through a generic service/controller hierarchy.
Inspected at commit ea981729a13e7e56a8d678c9292c6e00c3bbcf61.
limitations: This proves Reactor/Spring code in this library, not enterprise-wide RxJava or Vert.x use, deployed payment topology or suitability for Etail's architecture.

title: Building trust in AI-powered transactions with Amex Agentic Commerce Experiences
evidence: Amex engineering authors describe enrollment, structured intent, constrained credentials and asynchronous notifications. Partner authentication uses OAuth and mTLS; SDKs, Agent Skills, MCP and reference implementations are described as forthcoming.
limitations: The article describes a design and development direction. It does not establish public SDK availability, a complete API contract or general production availability.

title: US7835960B2 — System for facilitating a transaction
scope: Patent publication: proposed secondary transaction-number authorization and capture architecture
evidence: Published 2010-11-16; original assignee American Express Travel Related Services Co Inc. Figures 8, 9 and 12 describe secondary-number mapping, authorization checks and separate financial capture/AP/AR relationships.
limitations: Patent embodiments are not deployed-system evidence. Google Patents currently lists Liberty Peak Ventures LLC as assignee; legal status and ownership were not independently determined.
Historical security examples and optional business rules are not implementation recommendations.

title: US7962408B2 — Systems and methods for establishing an allocation of an amount between transaction accounts
scope: Patent publication: proposed allocation, transaction management and financial submission components
evidence: Published 2011-06-14; original assignee American Express Travel Related Services Co Inc. Figure 21 distinguishes a C2C service, transaction manager, business rules and financial transaction submission daemon.
limitations: This is a proposed embodiment, not current deployed topology. Google Patents lists Liberty Peak Ventures LLC as assignee; no legal determination is made.
Patent allocation/approval examples are not authority for Etail account access, liability or economic rules.

title: US20230206197A1 — Card to bank payments solution
scope: Patent application publication: proposed supplier payment routing and periodic reconciliation
evidence: Published 2023-06-29; original assignee American Express Travel Related Services Co Inc. The disclosure connects supplier identity/preferences, direct-account or virtual-number routing, reconciliation and remittance notifications.
limitations: An application publication is not a deployed product or available API. Google Patents labels the application abandoned, but that aggregate status was not independently legally verified.
No permission to implement patented subject matter or current commercial availability is inferred.
